item.title: Will the Bardella Scandal Sink Le Pen?
item.description: The scandal over antisemitic comments made by the far-right National Rally's Jordan Bardella could die down quickly, enabling Marine Le Pen to stick to her current plan: win the 2027 presidential election and name Bardella her prime minister. But there are two other possible scenarios, neither of which would be good for Bardella.

item.title: Can China and America Handle Being Ordinary?
item.description: For at least a generation, China's "economic miracle" allowed its people to look at Americans not as inhabitants of a richer world, but as potential peers. But now the two societies are peers in a different sense, because the Chinese are increasingly suffering the same rude awakening that Americans did when their own miracle ended.

item.title: What the US and China Should Discuss at APEC
item.description: Both sides are feeding an AI investment bubble – and Shenzhen is the place to talk about it.

item.title: How to Improve Global Mineral Governance
item.description: The race to secure critical minerals has intensified at the same time as the international community has recognized the need for more sustainable and responsible mining practices. Translating the resulting frameworks and guidelines into concrete action will require consolidating Global South policy and advocacy networks.

item.title: Australia’s Billionaire Problem and the ‘Corruption of the Democratic Process’
item.description: Australia’s incoming political finance laws will cap donations and electioneering spending for the first time, but the limits are generous, the rules complex, and the two-year delay suspiciously convenient for the major parties.

item.title: South Korea Recalls Ambassador, Demands Public Apology From Ukraine
item.description: A diplomatic rift is growing after a North Korean prisoner transfer that Kyiv revealed against Seoul’s wishes.

item.description: The admiration for Leo is based on his sporting exploits; the passion for Diego is rooted in culture and identity.

item.title: The China-EU Trade Truce Buys Time
item.description: For the EU, the choice is increasingly difficult: secure real concessions from Beijing to address structural trade imbalances or deploy stronger unilateral measures to protect its industrial base.

item.title: A Global Debt Crisis Is Looming
item.description: After a decade of debt accumulation, higher interest rates and growing refinancing needs have left the global economy increasingly exposed to shocks. And now ongoing conflicts are driving up energy prices, fueling renewed inflationary pressures and revealing dangerous cracks in the existing debt architecture.

item.title: Southeast Asia Has a Serious Drug Problem
item.description: Southeast Asia’s drug labs are pumping out unprecedented amounts of meth and other synthetic drugs.

item.title: Europe Must Look Beyond the US and China to Solve Its Productivity Problem
item.description: Given America and China’s lead in AI and other cutting-edge innovations, it is not surprising that much of the European economic policy debate revolves around the need to emulate and catch up with these two technological superpowers. In fact, neither the US nor China offers a relevant or attractive model for Europe.

item.title: Chinese Robots Could Decide the AI Race
item.description: Scott Singer and Pavlo Zvenyhorodsky, researchers at Carnegie’s China AI Initiative, argue that China is betting that AI dominance will come from combining hardware and software, or AI-powered robots. By focusing only on software such as AI models, they argue, Washington and Silicon Valley risk falling behind.

item.description: Why disengagement is not the answer.

item.title: To Rebuild the Nepali Congress, Gagan Thapa Must First Reform It
item.description: Recently re-elected president of the Nepali Congress, Thapa vowed to end the culture of nepotism and groupism in the party and to open it to a new generation of leaders.

item.title: Why Did the Industrial Revolution Not Start in India?
item.description: Due to abundant labor, its social structure, and the inertia of an economic system, there was little incentive to initiate mechanization and the Industrial Revolution in India.

item.title: Myanmar’s Min Aung Hlaing to Visit Indonesia and Brunei, Regime Spokesperson Says
item.description: Since taking office in April, the former general has visited five ASEAN member states as he seeks normalization with the Southeast Asian bloc.
